ruling.reasoning:
The trip was billed on 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km, a +4.2 km deviation, and the single off-route segment is F3 (21:43–21:50, 5.14 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.44 km, adding 3.70 km on Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road) [F1][F3][RD-1]. That is well over the 1 km tolerance, so the refund matrix in RD-2 is engaged [F4][RD-2].

The RD-4 screen is settled against a traffic justification: the Ayer Rajah Expressway — the replaced stretch — was in speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and Central Expressway in band 8 during the whole trip window, and no incident, closure or heavy congestion is recorded near the route [F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. The trace marks this ✗, so this is a no-traffic-reason case: the excess distance fare is refundable and a driver violation is recorded under RD-2 [RD-2].

Consent is the decisive element, and the record settles it. At 21:40 the driver asked, "mind if I go round via Telok Blangah Road?" [F7]; at 21:40 the rider refused: "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway" [F8]. Before the segment began at 21:43 the rider had therefore expressly ruled out the alternative, and there is no rider message consenting to it; the driver's account in F11 is a statement made after the trip, and a driver's claim of agreement is not the rider's consent [F11][RD-5]. The rider's 21:44 message, "Why you go this way?? I said stay," confirms there was no agreement [F9][RD-5]. The only consent question to read is whether the rider asked for or agreed to anything before 21:43:35, and the chat is a complete, fully timestamped 3-message record showing refusal, not agreement [F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. So the finding for F3 is consent_after_or_none → counts, under the named_road_elsewhere reading: Telok Blangah Road was not driven — the roads driven were Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road, Henderson Road [F3], and even if the words were read as a proposal the rider's "No" named no road he was permitted to use. No rider message names a stop, so RD-3 gives no exemption either; the driver's own chosen route to his own chosen end remains a deviation [F3][RD-3][RD-5].

Amount: 4.18 km deviation (billed distance − optimal route) less 0 km exempt = 4.18 km × $1.4098/km = $5.893... ≈ $5.89, consistent with the trace's refundable-km formula and the fare record [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded, and surge was 1.0× in any event [F5][F6][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint. They contain a route argument and mild frustration ("Why you go this way?? I said stay. I'm late already.") [F9], but no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; no accident or injury is described [F7][F8][F9][F11][F12][F14]. safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the GPS track, fare breakdown, timestamped complete chat and traffic record settle every element this ruling needs — deviation, consent and traffic reason — so evidence_status = sufficient.

That fails under RD-5: consent must be the rider's message before the segment, and the rider's 21:40 message refused the proposal [F8]; a post-trip statement of agreement [F11] is not consent, and the driver's own words admit he took the route anyway [F11]. Even read as a proposal to 'go via Telok Blangah Road', the agreed road must be driven on the segment: the roads driven were Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road only because the driver went his own way; the rider's words ruled the alternative out, so the segment is not covered by any agreement — RD-5 (no consent before the segment, no named road tied to the agreement).

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your dispute and you're getting a partial refund of $5.89. You were charged for 14.9 km, but the route should have been about 10.7 km. You told the driver before the detour that you did not agree to the longer way, and he took it anyway. Traffic did not explain the extra distance. The $5.89 goes back to the card or account you originally paid with; tolls, time and surge charges are not refunded. Nothing changes on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed this trip and found the route was longer than it should have been. The rider replied before the detour that he did not agree to the Telok Blangah Road way, and no traffic problem explains the extra distance. We are refunding the rider $5.89 to his original payment method, and recording a route violation on your account. You will also get a reminder about your duty to notify riders of route changes; the earlier notification issue is logged on your compliance record, not as a formal warning. No account flag.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first such incident); record a driver violation under RD-2 (no traffic reason) — no repeat breach, so no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was billed on 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km, a +4.2 km deviation, and the single off-route segment is F3 (21:43–21:50, 5.14 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.44 km, adding 3.70 km over Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road) [F1][F3][RD-1]. The deviation is over the 1 km tolerance, so the RD-2 matrix applies [F4][RD-2].

The traffic screen is settled against the driver: the replaced stretch, Ayer Rajah Expressway, was in speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) throughout the trip window, Central Expressway in band 8, and no incident, closure or heavy congestion is recorded [F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. The trace marks RD-4 ✗, so this is a no-traffic-reason case: excess distance fare refundable and a driver violation recorded [RD-2].

Consent is the decisive element and the record settles it. At 21:40 the driver asked, "mind if I go round via Telok Blangah Road?" [F7]; at 21:40 the rider answered "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway" [F8]. Before the segment began at 21:43 the rider had refused the alternative; the chat is complete and every message timestamped [F10]; and no rider message agrees. RD-5 requires the rider's own message sent before or at the start of the segment — a driver's account written after the trip is not consent, and here the driver's own words admit he took the route anyway [F11][RD-5]. The rider's 21:44 message, "Why you go this way?? I said stay," confirms there was no agreement [F9][RD-5]. The rider named no road he was agreeing to (he named one he ruled out), so nothing is tied to the segment; RD-3 gives no exemption because no rider message named a place the car went to and no stop was measured [F3][F7][F8][RD-3].

Amount: 4.18 km deviation (billed distance − optimal route) less 0 km exempt = 4.18 km × $1.4098/km = $5.893... ≈ $5.89, exactly the trace formula [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge was 1.0× in any event [F5][F6][RD-2].

Driver profile: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 flag_account is not triggered, and profile facts never decide the case [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint. They contain a route argument and mild frustration ("Why you go this way?? I said stay. I'm late already.") [F9], but no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and no accident or injury is described [F7][F8][F9][F11][F12][F14]. safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the GPS track, fare breakdown, complete timestamped chat and traffic record settle every element this ruling needs (deviation, consent, traffic reason), so evidence_status = sufficient.
